region: Stags Leap District · Napa Valley, California
about: Stags’ Leap Winery sits beneath the rocky palisades on the eastern edge of Napa Valley, in what is now the Stags Leap District. Its vineyard was first planted in 1893, when Horace Chase and his wife, Minnie Mizner Chase, founded the estate and built the stone Manor House that still anchors it. Frances Grange later ran the property as a working ranch and resort, Carl Doumani revived the winery from 1971, and today it belongs to Treasury Wine Estates, with Christophe Paubert as winemaker.

The Leap is the estate’s top Cabernet, a barrel selection drawn from the best blocks of the home vineyard, where the vines average about 30 years old. Higher up the slope the soils are thin and rocky; on the valley floor they turn to finer loam. Each lot macerates for close to a month and ages separately for 19 months in French oak, 65 percent new, before the winemakers choose the final blend just ahead of bottling. In 2020 that meant 92 percent Cabernet Sauvignon with small parts Petite Sirah, Malbec and Merlot.

The winery describes a deep ruby wine with red and dark berries and a note of wild lavender on the nose, then black cherry, black raspberry and plum touched with cola nut, root spice and espresso. It is full-bodied, with firm, chewy tannins and a long finish of graphite, mocha and dark chocolate. James Suckling suggested drinking it from 2027; the winery gives it 10 to 20 years of life.
facts: 92% Cabernet Sauvignon, 4% Petite Sirah, 3% Malbec, 1% Merlot
